stanza_to_reference_map.scene_summary: Vasudeva carries the infant through the swollen Yamuna under Adishesha; the flood and crossing are unmistakable.
stanza_to_reference_map.caption_text_exact: When Vasudeva set out carrying Baby Krishna, he saw the waters of the Yamuna river flooded to the skies.  As he crossed, the waters were reduced to the ankles of his feet as if it was an illusory flood caused by magic.

stanza_to_reference_map.scene_summary: Vasudeva is at the sleeping Yashoda/Nanda household with two infants, visually indicating the baby exchange.
stanza_to_reference_map.caption_text_exact: At Gokulam, everyone were fast asleep. Doors of Nandagopan's house opened and the Yogamaya gave a shrill cry as if to announce the location of the house. Vasudeva left  baby Krishna near sleeping Yashoda and carried the girl child to reach Mathura faster.

stanza_to_reference_map.scene_summary: A royal figure (Kamsa) enters the prison scene where Devaki holds the infant; matches the arrival after the cry.
stanza_to_reference_map.caption_text_exact: After reaching the prison,  the child’s (Yogamaya) crying sound made the guards rush to inform Kamsa that the 8th baby is born. Kamsa came running in anger and agitation to the prison cell, but was confused to see a baby girl in his sister Devaki's hands.

stanza_to_reference_map.scene_summary: Kamsa raises the infant girl to strike her against stone; matches the attempted killing.
stanza_to_reference_map.caption_text_exact: Kamsa thought to himself that this must be some maaya of Lord Vishnu. He snatched the baby from Devaki's hands like an elephant snatching and plucking the lotus from the pond and lifted his hand to hit it hard on the stone slab.

stanza_to_reference_map.scene_summary: Yogamaya appears aloft as a many-armed goddess with weapons; matches the eight-armed manifestation.
stanza_to_reference_map.caption_text_exact: The baby child, Yoga Maayaa freed herself from the clutches of Kamsa immediately. Not hitting the earth, she rose above the earth in the sky and took a divine form with powerful weapons in her eight arms.

stanza_to_reference_map.scene_summary: The goddess is shown suspended above Kamsa with devas around her; supports her warning and departure.
stanza_to_reference_map.caption_text_exact: Yogamaya called out to the cruel king Kamsa and said that there is no use in killing her, the person who is going to kill him is born elsewhere.  Yogamaaya then vanished in to the different temples in the earth while devas sprinkled flowers on her.

stanza_to_reference_map.scene_summary: A collage of demonic figures including a crowned king and monstrous/demonic forms supports Kamsa dispatching the asuras; image carries a visible stock watermark, but its numbered/caption context is clear.
stanza_to_reference_map.caption_text_exact:
Kamsa informed his demons Pralamba, Baka, and Poothana about Yogamaya's words. The asuras went around  killing all the male infants all around the world.
Merciless people are capable of doing merciless deeds.

stanza_to_reference_map.scene_summary: Both refs show newborn Krishna in Gokula amid celebrating women: 008 is a moonlit cradle gathering; 009 is a decorated cradle with festal offerings. 009 is also captioned #8, so it is a duplicate-numbered alternate for stanza 8, not an unsupported stanza.
stanza_to_reference_map.caption_text_exact: Bhagwan baby Krishna now gave a cry announcing his birth in Gokulam, waking up Yashoda. She immediately informed Nandagopan and all gopikas, the happy news of arrival of male child. The whole Gokula rejoiced the arrival of the child.

stanza_to_reference_map.scene_summary: Yashoda holds and gazes closely at the infant; it conveys the described maternal feeding/caressing moment, though nursing is not literally visible.
stanza_to_reference_map.caption_text_exact: Yasodha looked at baby Krishna who was as fresh as the kaayambu flower, fed him with milk, touched and caressed him and felt extremely happy.

stanza_to_reference_map.scene_summary: Nanda, infant, and assembled Brahmins/ritual offerings form a clear blessing and gift-giving scene; supports the captioned closing request.
stanza_to_reference_map.caption_text_exact:
Nandagopa, overwhelmed with joy distributed gifts to all holy Brahmins and performed all rituals for baby's welfare.

Bhattathiri requested Bhagwan who blesses auspiciousness to all in the three worlds to ward off his diseases and protect him.
